n: Continuing his Liberty Jail letter, Joseph suggests the Saints document everything they have suffered at the hands of Missourians. Careful records would support appeals for justice.
They should record property losses and damages—to reputation, body, and land.

f.g: Land and buildings, as opposed to movable goods.

n: They should also record the names of those involved in the oppression, as far as possible.
A committee might gather sworn statements and collect libelous publications. Hundreds of Saints later wrote such petitions, which were sent to Congress.

f.g: Falsely damaging to someone’s reputation in print.

n: They should gather negative reports from magazines, encyclopedias, and histories and present the full chain of wickedness done against the Saints.

These records should be published worldwide and presented to government leaders—a last required effort before the Saints could fully claim God’s promise to intervene, so the nation would be left without excuse.

f.w: present them to the heads of government

n: This is a solemn duty to God, angels, and families crushed by grief. Joseph traces the persecution to a spirit that has fastened inherited false creeds onto people’s hearts and filled the world with confusion.

f.w: the creeds of the fathers, who have inherited lies

f.g: The main driving spring of a clock; the chief cause.

n: Joseph piles up images of captivity—yoke, bands, handcuffs, chains, fetters—to show how such a spirit binds people.
The duty extends to widows and orphans whose husbands and fathers were killed—such as at the Hawn’s Mill massacre in October 1838.

f.g: About 17 Latter-day Saint men and boys were killed at Hawn’s Mill on October 30, 1838.

n: Such deeds are so dark they would make hell shudder and the devil’s hands tremble.
It is also a duty owed to the rising generation and to all the pure in heart.
Many good people in every church are blinded by others’ cunning and kept from truth only because they don’t know where to find it—a hopeful and generous view of other faiths.

f.w: only kept from the truth because they know not where to find it

n: So the Saints should spend their lives bringing hidden evils to light, as revealed from heaven.

f.w: bringing to light all the hidden things of darkness

n: These duties should be done with real earnestness.
Don’t treat these as small matters; much in the Saints’ future depends on them.
A memorable image: a small helm (rudder) steers a huge ship in a storm, keeping it “workways”—positioned to ride the wind and waves. Small acts can change great outcomes.

f.g: In a workable position; headed so the ship can handle the storm.

n: Do everything in our power cheerfully, and then stand still with full confidence to see God’s salvation—as Moses told Israel at the Red Sea.

f.w: let us cheerfully do all things that lie in our power
f.g: A widely quoted principle: do your part, then trust God.

f.w: stand still, with the utmost assurance, to see the salvation of God
